exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Linear Combination of Two Vectors

question.text: Given the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ shown above, which of the following could be the linear combination $2\mathbf{a}-2\mathbf{b}?$
question.explanation:
First, recall that

\[ 2\mathbf{a}-2\mathbf{b} = 2\mathbf{a} + (-2\mathbf{b}). \]

  • The vector $2\mathbf{a}$ has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$ but twice the magnitude.

  • The vector $-2\mathbf{b}$ has the direction that is opposite to $\mathbf{b}$ but twice the magnitude.

Now, we can draw $-2\mathbf{b}$ starting from the head of $2\mathbf{a}.$ The resultant \[ 2\mathbf{a}-2\mathbf{b} \] goes from the tail of $2\mathbf{a}$ to the head of $-2\mathbf{b}.$

example.title: Finding a Linear Combination of Two Vectors

question.text: Given the vectors $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$ shown above, which of the following could be the linear combination $-2\mathbf{p}-4\mathbf{q}?$
question.explanation:
First, recall that

\[ -2\mathbf{p}-4\mathbf{q} = -2\mathbf{p} + (-4\mathbf{q}). \]

  • The vector $-2\mathbf{p}$ has the direction that is opposite to $\mathbf{p}$ and $2$ times the magnitude.

  • The vector $-4\mathbf{q}$ has the direction that is opposite to $\mathbf{q}$ and $4$ times the magnitude.

Now, we can draw $-4\mathbf{q}$ starting from the head of $-2\mathbf{p}.$ The resultant \[ -2\mathbf{p}-4\mathbf{q} \] goes from the tail of $-2\mathbf{p}$ to the head of $-4\mathbf{q}.$

example.title: Finding a Linear Combination of Two Vectors

question.text: Given the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ shown above, which of the following could be the linear combination $-4\mathbf{a}-3\mathbf{b}?$
question.explanation:
First, recall that

\[ -4\mathbf{a}-3\mathbf{b} = -4\mathbf{a} + (-3\mathbf{b}). \]

  • The vector $-4\mathbf{a}$ has the direction that is opposite to $\mathbf{a}$ and $4$ times the magnitude.

  • The vector $-\mathbf{b}$ has the direction that is opposite to $\mathbf{b}$ and $3$ times the magnitude.

Now, we can draw $-3\mathbf{b}$ starting from the head of $-4\mathbf{a}.$ The resultant \[ -4\mathbf{a}-3\mathbf{b} \] goes from the tail of $-4\mathbf{a}$ to the head of $-3\mathbf{b}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Solving a Statement With Linear Combinations Whose Coefficients Are Linear Functions

question.text:
Suppose we are given two vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ where $\mathbf{a} \nparallel \mathbf{b}.$ Find $\lambda$ and $\mu,$ if 
\[
\mathbf{a} - 2\mathbf{b}=(3\lambda-\mu)\mathbf{a}-(\lambda-4\mu)\mathbf{b}.
\]
question.explanation:
Since $\mathbf{a} \nparallel \mathbf{b},$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. So, the coefficients of $\mathbf{a}$ must be equal, and the coefficients of $\mathbf{b}$ must be equal.

Equating the coefficients, we get: \[ \begin{cases} 3\lambda - \mu = 1 \\[5pt] \lambda - 4\mu = 2 \end{cases} \]

From the first equation, we obtain: \[ \mu= 3\lambda - 1 \]

Substituting back into the second equation, we get: \begin{align*} \lambda - 4\mu &= 2 \\[5pt] \lambda - 4(3\lambda - 1) &= 2 \\[5pt] \lambda - 12\lambda +4 &= 2 \\[5pt] -11\lambda &= -2 \\[5pt] \lambda &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{2}{11}} \end{align*}

Finally, we have \begin{align*} \mu&= 3\lambda -1 \\[5pt] &= 3\cdot \dfrac{2}{11}-1 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\dfrac{5}{11}}. \end{align*}

example.title: Solving a Statement With Linear Combinations Whose Coefficients Are Linear Functions

question.text: Suppose we are given two vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ where $\mathbf{a} \nparallel \mathbf{b}.$ Find $s$ and $t,$ if \[ 5\mathbf{a}+4\mathbf{b}=(2s+t)\mathbf{a}+(s-t)\mathbf{b}. \]
question.explanation:
Since $\mathbf{a} \nparallel \mathbf{b},$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. So, the coefficients of $\mathbf{a}$ must be equal, and the coefficients of $\mathbf{b}$ must be equal.

Equating the coefficients, we get: \[ \begin{cases} 2s+t=5\\ s-t=4 \end{cases} \]

Adding the equations, we obtain: \begin{align*} 3s&=9 \\ s&= 3 \end{align*}

Substituting back into the first equation, we get: \begin{align*} 2s+t &= 5 \\[3pt] 2(3) + t &= 5 \\[3pt] 6 + t &= 5 \\[3pt] t &=-1 \end{align*}

So, we conclude that $s = 3$ and $t = -1.$
